title: Deeper at constant width: 8 -> 10 layers, dim stays 512
description: DEPTH 8 -> 10 and ASPECT_RATIO 64 -> 48, so model_dim stays 512 with 4 heads of 128; two constants, nothing else touched.
reflection: POSITIVE and large: val_bpb 0.989238 vs baseline 0.997358, an improvement of 0.0081 -- roughly 9x the ~0.0009 noise floor measured in round 0, and the first real move of the cell. Capacity, not optimization, was the binding constraint, exactly as the two flat/negative axes (batch size, head split) implied. Cost side came in close to my estimate: FLOPs/token 2.39e8 -> 2.96e8 (+24%), tokens 412.6M -> 377.5M (-8.5%), steps 3148 -> 2880, params 50.3M -> 60.8M, peak VRAM 22.2 -> 27.2 GB. The token loss was smaller than the FLOP increase because the deeper model runs at higher steady-state MFU (37.46% vs 33.12%): more transformer work per step amortises the fixed per-step optimizer/Python overhead better. So depth is cheaper here than a naive FLOP count suggests, which is a compounding argument for pushing further. Open questions for the next round: (1) where does the capacity/token trade turn over -- DEPTH 12 (ASPECT_RATIO 40, dim still 512) is the obvious next probe, and VRAM headroom allows it; (2) widening instead of deepening is now also worth one probe, since the win says 'more parameters' and does not by itself say 'depth specifically'; (3) the epoch counter stayed at 1 in both runs, so we are not re-reading data and the capacity-over-tokens argument is not an artifact of repetition.
